questions.question: What are "Tier 2 words"?
options: High-utility academic vocabulary used across subjects, like "analyze" and "significant"
Basic everyday words like "house" and "dog"
Highly technical terms used in only one subject
Slang words used by teenagers
questions.explanation: Tier 2 words are academic words useful across many subjects — analyze, demonstrate, significant, consequently.

questions.question: What is hedging in academic writing?
options: Softening claims with words like "may", "might" and "suggests"
Hiding your opinion completely
Using as many strong claims as possible
Quoting without citing
questions.explanation: Hedging shows appropriate academic caution: "The results suggest..." rather than "This proves...".

questions.question: Which feature is typical of academic register?
options: Avoiding contractions and slang in favour of precise, formal vocabulary
Frequent use of emojis
Short text-message style sentences
Casual jokes to engage the reader
questions.explanation: Academic register avoids contractions, slang and overly personal statements, favouring precision and objectivity.

questions.question: Why is learning academic language important?
options: It is required for school, higher education and professional contexts
It replaces everyday English completely
It is only needed by professors
It makes texts longer automatically
questions.explanation: Academic language is essential for assignments, higher education and professional life, and helps express complex ideas clearly.

questions.question: Which sentence shows correct conversion from informal to academic register?
options: "Kids use phones a lot" becomes "Young people use mobile devices extensively"
"Young people use mobile devices extensively" becomes "Kids use phones a lot"
"Kids use phones a lot" becomes "Kids really use phones loads"
"Young people use mobile devices" becomes "OMG everyone is on their phone"
questions.explanation: Academic register replaces informal words (kids, a lot) with precise, formal equivalents (young people, extensively).
